texts.facts: 1. This is a criminal revision petition u/s 397/399 Cr.P.C. filed against order dated 24.02.2021 passed by the court of Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate (NI Act), Digital Court-02/SED in Criminal Complaint No. 526/2021 titled as IFCI Factors Limited Through Authorized Representative Vs. Critical Mass Multilink Ltd., whereby the revisionist and some others were summoned to face trial for the commission of offence punishable u/s 138 Negotiable Instruments Act (hereinafter referred to NI Act). Grounds of Revision Crl. Revision No: 404/2024 Pawan Kumar Agrawal Vs. IFCI Factors Ltd. page no. 2 of 21 3. Therefore the petitioner herein is not liable to be proceeded against under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and the summoning order and the complaint filed by respondent is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] order on this ground alone. B. Because the Ld. MM has failed to consider that if the offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 is by a Company then in that case principles of Section 141 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 have to be followed and as per Section 141 in case of offence by Company only those persons who are in charge of the Company or who conduct the business of the Company are liable for the Acts of the company and ora liable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. Therefore applying the above test it is very clear that since the petitioner had resigned from the Company on Crl. Revision No: 404/2024 Pawan Kumar Agrawal Vs. IFCI Factors Ltd. page no. 3 of 21 22.11.2017 and the cheque has been presented / dishonour on 20.11.2020 i.e. after almost more than three year of the resignation of the petitioner, then since the petitioner was not in charge of the business of the Critical Mass Multilink ltd Company, he cannot be proceeded against under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
texts.arguments: Therefore since in the present case admittedly the petitioner herein has resigned from the Company on 22.11.2017 and the same has been accepted by the Company on 22.11.2017, therefore the petitioner cannot be held liable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 for any offence committed by the Company.
